**It falls out of step 1, on the same sheet.** Any impact dimension scored 4 resolves to **Level 4
BCA** at every likelihood, so the designation is a consequence of the impact assessment rather than
a separate judgement made alongside it. You do not decide it here; you read it.

Level 4 BCA is the whole top row of the matrix, and nothing below impact 4 reaches it however likely
an error is. That is the point: Business Critical is about what an error would do, not about how
hard the work is.

Level 4 adds to Level 3 rather than replacing it: formal audits, external review, additional
scrutiny of the documentation, scrutiny of the structural and conceptual assumptions, and additional
scenario testing. It also brings a named Analysis Senior Responsible Officer and an entry on the
register.

**A Very High rating in the risk framework is a backstop, not a second route in.** The Analytical
Risk Assessment and Quality Assurance Framework lists escalation to Business Critical Analysis
separately, with four triggers joined by "and/or", of which a Very High rating is one. Treat it as a
check on the scoring rather than as a designation in itself: a Very High rating on work not
designated at scoping means the impact dimensions should be scored again with the commissioner.
